architecture.style: Server-rendered PHP web application with role-specific page modules, shared helper/service includes and JSON endpoints; a three-layer logical description is appropriate, but this is not a separated microservice or formal MVC deployment.
architecture.presentation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript pages in root, user/, staff/, admin/ and rider/; browser camera/geolocation/notifications plus polling for updates.
architecture.application: PHP page handlers coordinate validation, authentication, pricing, payment workflow and status updates; config helpers supply storage, encryption, inventory, loyalty, settings and audit behavior.
architecture.data: mysqli-compatible DBCompatConnection/Statement/Result wrappers connect to a configured MySQL/MariaDB database; local upload and QR files live under application root.

security.implementation: PHP password_hash(PASSWORD_DEFAULT) and password_verify; successful privileged login regenerates session ID. Separate role-session identities allow admin, staff and rider portals in one browser.

AES-256-GCM uses 32-byte key, random 12-byte nonce and 16-byte authentication tag; encoded as enc:v1: plus Base64(nonce||tag||ciphertext). Selected personal fields and settings are encryption targets, not every database value.

HMAC-SHA-256 of trimmed lowercase UTF-8 input creates CHAR(64) deterministic lookup values for username/contact matching. Decryption occurs in DBCompatResult.fetch_assoc, including prepared statement results.

Prepared statements are used on selected paths, alongside real_escape_string and sanitize in legacy queries; HTML output frequently uses htmlspecialchars. This is evidence of controls, not blanket proof against injection or XSS.

Payment-proof handlers check upload status, a 5 MB size limit, getimagesize and allowlisted JPEG/PNG/WebP. Storage utility confines object paths to uploads/ or qrcodes/ and rejects traversal segments. Logo upload also checks CSRF token and file MIME.
Request logs record actor, action, page, method, IP, user agent and allowlisted request metadata; selected frequent polling and CLI requests are excluded.
Order reservation, stock release, staff approval and annual reset use begin_transaction, FOR UPDATE, commit and rollback on relevant paths.

algorithms.name: Order pricing
algorithms.formula: unit_price = configured_water_price[size] + (new_container ? configured_container_price[size] : 0); subtotal = quantity * unit_price; discount = 5 * floor(quantity / 5); delivery_fee = delivery and no approved free-delivery reward ? 10 * quantity : 0; total = subtotal + delivery_fee - discount.
algorithms.notes: Amounts in PHP. Formula from server purchase path; current configured prices may override defaults. Quantity counts ordered containers, although UI/settings sometimes say gallons.

algorithms.name: Stock reservation and release
steps: Validate item size, quantity and fulfillment option.
Begin transaction and lock applicable inventory row; for a new container also lock the generic New Container item.
Reject insufficient stock; otherwise deduct quantity, record movement and reservation references, and save pending order.
Editing releases old stock before reserving replacement stock; denial releases reserved stock.
Staff approval locks pending order, performs legacy stock reservation when needed, and commits status and loyalty changes.

algorithms.name: Queue priority
algorithms.formula: ORDER BY qr_priority DESC, created_at ASC, id ASC
algorithms.notes: QR-scanned orders have priority; within equal priority orders follow creation time then numeric ID. This is deterministic sorting, not an optimization or AI model.

algorithms.name: Loyalty accrual
algorithms.notes: Default rate is 1; setting is clamped to 0..100. Points are awarded on staff approval, not immediately on checkout. The calculation uses number of ordered containers; it does not multiply by the physical gallon capacity.

algorithms.name: Annual loyalty reset
steps: If missing/invalid, store one year from current server date.
When due, lock setting in a transaction, zero all customer points and set points_year to current year.
Advance scheduled date one year and repeat if multiple anniversaries passed.
algorithms.notes: System-wide anniversary, triggered by application requests; not a per-customer signup anniversary and not a scheduled cron job in reviewed implementation.

algorithms.name: Reward conversion
steps: Check selected reward is enabled and customer has enough points.
Create zero-value reward transaction and pending reward_claim.
Staff approves claim; approved free-delivery reward is later locked and consumed during checkout.
algorithms.notes: General redemption deduction/logging is not enclosed in a DB transaction in user/rewards.php. Do not claim fully atomic redemption. Reward catalog currently contains six items with 50, 100, 125, 150, 200 and 250 point requirements.

algorithms.name: GPS display and latest-location selection
steps: Browser geolocation supplies rider coordinates to the application.
Store latitude, longitude and available accuracy/speed/heading; retrieve latest row by last_update then ID.
Customer map polls and redraws rider marker, destination pin and straight dashed connector.
algorithms.notes: Map connector is a visual straight line; no route optimization or guaranteed ETA algorithm was identified. Destination validation requires finite numeric latitude in [-90,90] and longitude in [-180,180].

algorithms.name: Random identifiers
algorithms.implementation: General IDs use a prefix plus 8 random bytes represented in uppercase hex. Customer and reward IDs use 4 random bytes with up to 10 database collision checks.

caveats.detail: Static code/schema review only. No runtime records, secrets, live schema introspection, migrations, benchmark or penetration test were used. Describe schema as code-defined and deployment-dependent.

19 distinct tables identified: 14 baseline and 5 runtime additions. CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not reconcile existing column types, indexes, defaults or foreign keys. Effective schema depends on installation history. Baseline FK declarations must not be presented as universally enforced.

Baseline transactions.delivery_status ENUM lacks ready_for_pickup and on_the_way values used by newer code. Runtime ADD IF NOT EXISTS does not change an existing ENUM. Verify/migrate deployment schema before treating pickup state persistence as confirmed.

Runtime users CREATE omits address but later MODIFY assumes it exists; runtime password NOT NULL and username UNIQUE differ from baseline nullable credential columns. Customer registration inserts no password. Do not claim database.php alone is a validated fresh installation path.

Hard-coded fallback credentials remain in rider login and administrator current-password checking. Do not repeat values in documentation or claim password verification is the only accepted credential path.

api/delivery_tracker.php dispatches read/write operations without a session/ownership gate and sends wildcard CORS. Several customer paths load records using supplied user_id or mobile lookup. Authorization and uniform CSRF coverage require review before deployment.

Only explicitly encrypted fields are protected at rest; notes, operational IDs, notification messages, audit actor names, payment fields and uploads are not universally encrypted. Lookup columns have no declared unique indexes; ciphertext uniqueness does not guarantee logical plaintext uniqueness. Legacy plaintext is accepted until migrated.

Code supports environment injection and a local key-file fallback. No key content was read. Deployment should protect and back up the key with restricted access; key rotation was not implemented in reviewed helper.

Redemption balance check/deduction and logging are not transactional, unlike stock approval; simultaneous requests may require further safeguards. Cancellation path does not explicitly reverse previously awarded loyalty points.

E-wallet payment is implemented using account/QR presentation, reference and screenshot submission, followed by local verification state. No direct GCash/Maya payment-gateway settlement API was identified in reviewed payment paths.

Most core entities are separated, but payment attributes repeat in transactions/payments, display notes contain embedded business details, and rider sender/recipient and audit actors are polymorphic. Avoid an unsupported claim of fully normalized 3NF.
